main.title: Resonance of Fate
main.summary: tri-Ace's role-playing game follows three mercenaries in Basel, with firearm battles built around movement, charging attacks and coordinated Hero actions.

cards.heading: Mercenaries live beneath the tower of Basel
cards.text: Sega released tri-Ace's Resonance of Fate for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in 2010. Zephyr, Leanne and Vashyron take mercenary jobs in Basel, a tower settlement built around a system that purifies a polluted Earth. Its mechanical core, Zenith, binds human lives to quartz stones. Their work draws the trio into the plans of the ruling Cardinals.

cards.heading: Scratch damage becomes a finishing shot
cards.text: Combat mixes turns with movement and charging attacks. Moving closer reduces the time needed to prepare a shot, but also exposes the character to danger. The player can wait for a stronger attack or interrupt an enemy preparing its own. Weapons divide the work: submachine guns quickly accumulate scratch damage but cannot deliver a kill. Pistols and grenades convert that accumulated damage into a direct result. Planning a turn therefore means considering position, timing and which character should set up the target for the next one.

cards.heading: Hero actions turn movement into gunplay
cards.text: Players are able to move around the battlefield freely, but they have the option to create predefined paths for the character to follow. While moving along these paths, characters gain access to Hero actions, which make them immune to damage and speed up charge times. However, the use of these Hero actions requires the use of Bezels; these items are an essential element in battle and are recharged through a variety of methods, such as destroying portions of an enemy's weapons and armor, or killing an enemy. Characters using Hero actions can attack while jumping in the air, and are also able to unleash special attacks which manifest as stylish firearm maneuvers. Enemies are only able to move while the player's current character is moving and will usually attack only that character.

cards.heading: tri-Ace builds cinematic combat around firearms
cards.text: The team wanted cinematic action to continue through battles rather than remain confined to cutscenes. Guns and movement offered a different language from familiar swords and magic, with films such as The Matrix informing the approach. Early experiments allowed direct control of one character while artificial intelligence handled the others. Testing exposed problems, including companions dying outside the player's view. Giving the player more strategic control helped reconcile the spectacle with responsibility for the whole party, turning the choreography into decisions rather than a performance watched from the sidelines.

cards.heading: Motoi Sakuraba and Kohei Tanaka contrast their musical worlds
cards.text: Motoi Sakuraba and K?hei Tanaka composed contrasting parts of the score. Sakuraba handled battle music with rock elements and analogue synthesizer sounds, sometimes processing electric piano and other instruments through Leslie speakers. Tanaka wrote for towns, cutscenes and the title theme, using an orchestral approach recorded with studio musicians at Hitomi Memorial Hall.

main.title: Dante's Inferno
main.subtitle: An action descent through Hell
main.summary: Dante's Inferno reshapes the Divine Comedy as an action game. Its descent through Hell combines scythe combat, mythic creatures and monumental environments, turning a literary journey into a physical ordeal.

cards.heading: Dante becomes a warrior
cards.text: Visceral Games reimagines the first part of The Divine Comedy as an action adventure. Its Dante becomes a warrior descending into Hell to save Beatrice. The poem's journey through distinct regions supplies an ordered route, while combat and obstacles turn each stage of the descent into a place the player must cross.

cards.heading: The circles of Hell
cards.text: The journey passes through Limbo, Lust, Gluttony, Greed, Anger, Heresy, Violence, Fraud and Treachery. Each circle has different environments, creatures and music. The artists and designers use those differences to give the next region a recognisable character as Dante descends.

cards.heading: Scythe, cross and progression
cards.text: Death's scythe and a holy cross provide the main combat options. Punishing or absolving certain souls develops different progression paths and unlocks abilities. These choices carry the religious imagery into the attacks and improvements available to the player.

main.title: BioShock 2
main.subtitle: Subject Delta and Big Daddy: perspective and point of view
main.summary: Rapture returns through the eyes of Subject Delta, a Big Daddy linked to a Little Sister. Weapons and plasmids work together, while protecting a vulnerable companion changes the rhythm of exploration and combat.

cards.heading: BioShock 2
cards.text: BioShock 2 returns to Rapture through Subject Delta, a Big Daddy linked to a Little Sister. The drill and weapons can be combined with plasmid powers, turning familiar corridors into spaces for preparing traps, controlling crowds and protecting a vulnerable companion.

cards.heading: Inside a Big Daddy
cards.text: BioShock 2 is a first-person shooter. The player assumes the character of silent protagonist Subject Delta eight years after the events of BioShock. The player explores Rapture and fights off Splicers using weapons, environmental hazards, and plasmids. Plasmids grant powers such as telekinesis and must be recharged with "EVE" before further use. The player can equip tonics—passive bonuses varying from increased speed to reduced EVE usage. Several weapons in BioShock 2 are unique to the Big Daddy, including a powerful drill and a rivet gun. The player can use each weapon in a close-range melee attack, and may simultaneously equip a weapon and a plasmid. If the player is killed, they are revived via a Vita-Chamber.

cards.heading: Rethinking familiar systems
cards.text: Some game mechanics were streamlined from BioShock, such as hacking into security systems and turrets. This is represented by a lengthy Pipe Mania–style minigame in BioShock, but a shorter timing puzzle in BioShock 2. The player stops a needle on a colored gauge; stopping on the gauge's green area completes the hack, and hitting small blue areas gives a bonus. If the needle lands on the white or red portions, the hack fails and damages the player or triggers an alarm. The research camera mechanic was altered, recording video instead of stills. Using it while damaging enemies in creative ways gives players bonuses or new abilities.

cards.heading: Protecting a Little Sister
cards.text: ADAM is used to upgrade the player's plasmids and tonics. Upgraded plasmids bestow additional abilities for more tactical usage; for example, an upgraded Electro Bolt plasmid inflicts chains of electric damage between enemies, rather than affecting only a single target. As a Big Daddy, the player can defeat other Big Daddies and either adopt their Little Sisters—having them gather ADAM for the player—or harvest the Sisters for their ADAM outright. After adopting a Little Sister, the player escorts her to corpses littered around Rapture and must protect her while she harvests more ADAM. Once the Little Sister has collected enough ADAM, the player can choose to either harvest or save her. Harvesting or saving Little Sisters will provoke attacks from Big Sisters. ADAM can also be collected from slugs when venturing into the open ocean surrounding Rapture.

main.title: Heavy Rain
main.summary: Heavy Rain is a 2010 action-adventure video game developed by Quantic Dream and published by Sony Computer Entertainment.

cards.heading: Four lives and the Origami Killer
cards.text: Heavy Rain is a 2010 action-adventure video game developed by Quantic Dream and published by Sony Computer Entertainment. The game features four protagonists involved with the mystery of the Origami Killer, a serial killer who uses extended periods of rainfall to drown his victims. The player interacts with the game by performing actions highlighted on screen related to motions on the controller, and in some cases, performing a series of quick time events. The player's choices and actions during the game affect the narrative.

cards.heading: Quantic Dream develops Heavy Rain
cards.text: Game developer David Cage wrote the 2,000-page script, acted as director for the four years of development, travelled to Philadelphia to research the setting, and intended to improve upon what was flawed in his 2005 game Fahrenheit. Composer Normand Corbeil wrote the score, which was recorded at Abbey Road Studios. The game was released for PlayStation 3 in February 2010, PlayStation 4 in 2016, and Windows in 2019. A critical and commercial success, Heavy Rain is considered one of the best video games ever made, receiving praise for its emotional impact, visuals, writing, controls, and music, though some critics faulted the controls, voice acting, and plot inconsistencies. It sold 5.3 million units by January 2018.

main.title: Battlefield: Bad Company 2
main.subtitle: Return to Bad Company
main.summary: DICE returns to Bad Company with squad roles, vehicles and destructible environments on PC and home consoles.

cards.heading: Return to Bad Company
cards.text: DICE developed Battlefield: Bad Company 2, published by Electronic Arts for Windows, PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in March 2010. It continues Bad Company's combination of infantry combat and vehicles, with destruction changing the cover available on the battlefield.

cards.heading: Gunfire reshapes the battlefield
cards.text:
While Bad Company 2 is primarily a first-person shooter, it follows other games in the series by allowing the player to control certain vehicles, including ATVs, APCs, tanks, and helicopters. On foot, players are given access to a variety of real-world small arms such as assault rifles and machine guns. Players can also jump, crouch, and sprint. They can carry one primary weapon and a pistol in multiplayer, or two primary weapons in single-player, as well as grenades and other equipment. Players can fire "from the hip", but zooming in and using iron sights, reflex sights, or telescopic sights (depending on the weapon) will provide much better accuracy when shooting.

Bad Company 2 heavily emphasizes destructible environments. Large sections of most buildings can be destroyed by explosives, and some walls and fences break down under barrages of bullets, with the game's physics engine realistically simulating the destruction.

cards.heading: Four roles keep a squad together
cards.text: Multiplayer is class-based, with four classes: Assault, Engineer, Medic, and Recon. Each class has a variety of unique weapons and equipment, and serves a specific role in combat. There are also some weapons that can be used by any class, such as pistols and shotguns. Each class gains experience and levels up separately.

main.title: Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs
main.subtitle: A new assignment across the islands
main.summary: Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs is Creatures' third Nintendo DS adventure about befriending Pokémon through the Capture Styler. Set in the island region of Oblivia, it follows the Ranger's efforts to stop the Pokémon Pinchers, with a ukulele-playing Pichu as a companion. The familiar loop-drawing action returns alongside new symbols that summon legendary helpers. The islands give those partnerships a larger physical role in travel. A creature's help can now become a way of crossing the region as well as overcoming the obstacle directly in front of the Ranger.

cards.heading: A new assignment across the islands
cards.text: Pokémon Ranger: Guardian Signs is Creatures' third Nintendo DS adventure about befriending Pokémon through the Capture Styler. Set in the island region of Oblivia, it follows the Ranger's efforts to stop the Pokémon Pinchers, with a ukulele-playing Pichu as a companion. The familiar loop-drawing action returns alongside new symbols that summon legendary helpers. The islands give those partnerships a larger physical role in travel. A creature's help can now become a way of crossing the region as well as overcoming the obstacle directly in front of the Ranger.

cards.heading: A sign calls a legendary partner
cards.text: Drawing the appropriate Guardian Sign summons a Legendary Pokémon such as Raikou, Entei or Suicune for use outside captures. The gesture connects a remembered pattern to a particular form of help. Ordinary encounters still ask for circles around moving targets, with attacks threatening the Styler's energy and experience improving its capabilities. The new signs add another kind of drawing to that familiar routine. Instead of only tracing around what is already visible, the player can use a symbol to call a useful presence into the journey.

cards.heading: An assignment that can be shared
cards.text: Separate cooperative missions allow up to four players to take part together, extending the Ranger idea beyond the main single-player story. Pokémon can also be brought into a capture to provide support, so help is represented through both the creatures and other human participants. The ukulele Pichu gives the main journey a distinctive travelling companion. Guardian Signs develops the series through these different scales of cooperation: a small ally at the Ranger's side, a legendary mount for the wider region and a group of players working through a shared assignment.

main.title: No Heroes Allowed!
main.subtitle: Build the dungeon the hero is trying to conquer
main.summary: No Heroes Allowed! is Japan Studio and Acquire's PSP strategy game, first released in Japan on 11 March 2010. The player digs a dungeon and encourages monsters to develop within it, defending the demon lord from approaching adventurers. The usual role-playing objective is reversed: the heroic intruder is the problem to be solved. The maze has to support the creatures that protect it as well as delay the visitors. A successful defence therefore begins long before the hero arrives, through the shape of the tunnels and the life the player allows to grow inside them.

cards.heading: Build the dungeon the hero is trying to conquer
cards.text: No Heroes Allowed! is Japan Studio and Acquire's PSP strategy game, first released in Japan on 11 March 2010. The player digs a dungeon and encourages monsters to develop within it, defending the demon lord from approaching adventurers. The usual role-playing objective is reversed: the heroic intruder is the problem to be solved. The maze has to support the creatures that protect it as well as delay the visitors. A successful defence therefore begins long before the hero arrives, through the shape of the tunnels and the life the player allows to grow inside them.

cards.heading: A monster needs an ecosystem, not only a room
cards.text: Digging changes the underground environment, creating routes and opportunities for different creatures. The player manages that system indirectly, relying on the inhabitants to confront the heroes rather than controlling each fighter individually. Water and aquatic monsters expand the possibilities in this third entry, adding another condition to the dungeon's design. A new passage can help the defence or give an invader a more convenient route, so every opening needs a purpose. The challenge lies in arranging an environment whose inhabitants can do useful work once the player is no longer deciding every movement.

cards.heading: A clearer name for a mischievous series
cards.text: The Japanese title presents it as the third What Did I Do to Deserve This, My Lord? game, while the Western name makes its reversed premise immediately clear. Badman's daughter Badnella joins the cast and supports a multiplayer mode built around the pair. North America received a digital edition in November 2010. Later PlayStation reissues kept the original PSP game available. Its humour and strategy share the same foundation: the familiar dungeon is understood from the other side, where an efficient hero is a destructive intruder and a healthy monster population is something worth protecting.

main.title: God of War III
main.summary: God of War III is a 2010 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment.

cards.text: Santa Monica Studio released God of War III for PlayStation 3 on March 16, 2010. Continuing God of War II, Kratos attacks Mount Olympus in pursuit of Zeus. After Gaia abandons him, Athena's spirit guides him towards Pandora, whose role is essential to opening Pandora's Box. The journey brings battles with gods, monsters and Titans.

The gameplay is similar to previous installments, focusing on combo-based combat with the player's main weapon—the Blades of Exile—and secondary weapons acquired during the game. It uses quick time events, where the player acts in a timed sequence to defeat strong enemies and bosses. The player can use up to four magical attacks and a power-enhancing ability as alternative combat options, and the game features puzzles and platforming elements. Compared with previous installments, God of War III offers a revamped magic system, more enemies, new camera angles, and downloadable content.

God of War III received large critical acclaim upon release, with praise for the graphics, gameplay, and scope, although the plot received a mixed response. The game received several awards, including "Most Anticipated Game of 2010" and "Best PS3 Game" at the 2009 and 2010 Spike Video Game Awards, respectively, the "Artistic Achievement" award at the 2011 British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA) Video Game Awards, and "Outstanding Achievement in Animation" at the 2011 Interactive Achievement Awards. One of the best-selling games in the God of War series and the ninth best-selling PlayStation 3 game of all time, it sold over 5 million copies worldwide by June 2012 and was included in the God of War Saga released for PlayStation 3 on August 28, 2012.

God of War III Remastered reached PlayStation 4 in July 2015 for the series' tenth anniversary. After additional prequels, the 2018 God of War continued Kratos' story in a setting drawn from Norse mythology.

main.title: Metro 2033
main.summary: Metro 2033 is a 2010 first-person shooter survival horror video game developed by 4A Games and published by THQ.

cards.text: Metro 2033 is a 2010 first-person shooter survival horror video game developed by 4A Games and published by THQ. The story is based on Dmitry Glukhovsky's novel of the same name, where survivors of a nuclear war have taken refuge in the Metro tunnels of Moscow. The player controls the silent protagonist Artyom, a man who must save his home station from the dangers lurking within the Metro. In the game, the player encounters human and mutant enemies, who can be killed with a variety of firearms. They must also wear a gas mask to explore areas covered in nuclear radiation, both underground and on the surface.

Metro 2033 was the debut title for 4A Games, whose founders had experience working on S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl at GSC Game World. Glukhovsky chose 4A Games to adapt his novel due to the studio's location in Ukraine, and their expertise in developing first-person shooters. Glukhovsky gave the studio much creative freedom. 4A Games focused their efforts on storytelling and atmosphere, intentionally avoiding any multiplayer gameplay to achieve their goal. The game was powered by the studio's own proprietary 4A Engine. It was first announced in 2006 as Metro 2033: The Last Refuge.

The game was released in March 2010 for Microsoft Windows and Xbox 360. Critics gave the game positive reviews, with praise for its horror elements, detailed environments, and interesting plot. However, the game was also criticized for its bugs and artificial intelligence. Metro 2033 was profitable for THQ, selling more than 1.5 million copies by June 2012, though the publisher felt that their marketing efforts were rushed. A sequel titled Metro: Last Light was released in 2013, with Deep Silver acquiring the publishing rights from THQ after their bankruptcy. A remastered version titled Metro 2033 Redux was released in 2014 for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. The remastered version was also included as part of a compilation titled Metro Redux containing both Metro 2033 Redux and Metro: Last Light Redux. A third installment, Metro Exodus, was released in 2019.

main.title: Yakuza 4
main.summary: Yakuza 4 is a 2010 action-adventure game developed and published by Sega for the PlayStation 3. The sequel to Yakuza 3 and the fourth main installment in the Yakuza series, it was released in Japan in March 2010 and internationally in March 2011.

cards.heading: Four perspectives open up Kamurocho
cards.text:
Yakuza 4 is a 2010 action-adventure game developed and published by Sega for the PlayStation 3. The sequel to Yakuza 3 and the fourth main installment in the Yakuza series, it was released in Japan in March 2010 and internationally in March 2011.

Yakuza 4 takes place one year after the events of Yakuza 3. Like the original game, most of the action takes place in Kamurocho (resembling Shinjuku's red-light district, Kabukichō). Three locations have been added since Yakuza 3: a rooftop area stretching across a large portion of the town, the back streets of Kamurocho (known as Rojiura) and a third area known as the underground (or "chika", which includes the city's sewers, parking lot and shopping arcades). The underground area is also known as Kamuchika, short for Kamuro Chika (Kamuro underground).

cards.heading: Four fighting styles reshape the same streets
cards.text: Each character has his own style of fighting and special moves as their body frames are different. Kiryu focuses on the powerful blows of Karate and Boxing, Akiyama prefers swift attacks using Taekwondo, Saejima favors powerful and slow brawling/grappling attacks using wrestling techniques, and Tanimura uses the defensive maneuvers of Aikido and Jiu Jitsu that he learned from his time at the police academy.

cards.heading: Side activities give each protagonist a different role
cards.text:
The available mini-games are pachinko, fishing, onsen, massage, table tennis, hanafuda and karaoke, including duets with non-player characters (NPCs). In Haruka's Wish, the player must raise Haruka's trust level. Each main character has a side game or goal which must be completed, and many side games are related to trophies.

Saejima's mission, Create a Fighter! is to train fighters to win tournaments after 50 rounds or less of training (building up movesets). Different movesets allow different moves to be performed.

Tanimura's mission, Resolving Police-Radio Disputes, is to keep the peace on the streets of Kamurocho. Radio reports tell him where to find incidents, and the player must defeat the perpetrator. In Kiryu's mission, Team Encounter Battle, seven gangs attack him and he must fight to reach each gang leader.

cards.heading: Butterfly City opens the Japanese edition
cards.text: The Japanese opening theme, "Butterfly City", features Zeebra, Ryo the Skywalker, Mummy-D and Double, with music by DJ Hasebe. Ariola Japan released the single on March 17, 2010. The international edition replaces the licensed Japanese songs with original music.
